title: Uranium and phosphate resources in the Cooper Formation of the Charleston region, South Carolina
citation: Force, E.R., Gohn, G.S., Force, L.M., and Higgins, B.B., 1978, Uranium and phosphate resources in the Cooper Formation of the Charleston region, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report OF-78-586, map scale 1:150,000.
notes: Plate 1 (page 1) is an OCR map image; only its legend is legible. Table 2 (pages 15-19) text layer is partly garbled: rows record depth, U (ppm), P2O5 (%) and comment; the surface elevation and depth-to-top-of-Cooper columns are read only where clear. Interval descriptions quote the table row verbatim (U ppm and P2O5 % values). Rows from Malde (1959) table 4 (page 18, unlabeled holes), EF 39C/40C/40B outcrops and AH 4/AH 18/AH59 were skipped because their columns are scrambled. Uranium and phosphate grades are recorded in descriptions; the schema has no chemistry fields.

name.quote: Phosphate deposits formerly exploited in the Charleston district were formed

rank.quote: by weathering and reworking of the Cooper Formation (Eocene and Oliogcene).

age.quote: by weathering and reworking of the Cooper Formation (Eocene and Oliogcene).

thickness.value: upper 48 m late Oligocene and lower 14 m late Eocene at Clubhouse Crossroads
thickness.quote:
At Clubhouse
Crossroads, the upper 48 m of the Cooper is of late Oligocene age, whereas the
lower 14 m is of late Eocene age.

contacts.value: overlies the Santee Limestone (Eocene); unconformably overlain by Pleistocene, Holocene, and locally upper Tertiary deposits; top is a subareal erosional surface in most places
contacts.quote:
The Cooper Formation overlies the Santee Limestone, (Eocene), and both
are unconformably overlain by Pleistocene, Holocene, and locally upper Tertiary

description.value: depth to Cooper ranges from 0 to 20 m; old Charleston mining district is on an erosional high in the vicinity of the Ashley River
description.quote:
Contours on the top of the Cooper Formation show that depth to Cooper ranges
from 0 to 20 m.
